claims.text: The prevalence of user reports indicative of LLM hallucinations is approximately 1.75% within mobile app reviews initially flagged as relevant to AI errors.
User-perceived LLM hallucinations in mobile apps can be categorized into a taxonomy of seven distinct types.
Factual Incorrectness (H1) is the most frequently reported LLM hallucination type in mobile app reviews, accounting for 38% of instances.
Nonsensical/Irrelevant Output (H3) accounts for 25% of user-reported LLM hallucination instances in mobile app reviews.
Fabricated Information (H2) accounts for 15% of user-reported LLM hallucination instances in mobile app reviews.
Mobile app reviews reporting LLM hallucinations show significantly lower VADER sentiment scores.

evidence.description: Analysis of candidate reviews estimated prevalence at approximately 1.75% within reviews flagged as relevant to AI errors.
Manual annotation of 1,000 candidate reviews resulted in a data-driven taxonomy of seven hallucination types.
Manual annotation data showed Factual Incorrectness (H1) emerged as the top reported type at 38%.
Manual annotation data showed Nonsensical/Irrelevant Output (H3) was the second most frequent type at 25%.
Manual annotation data showed Fabricated Information (H2) accounted for 15% of instances.
Sentiment characteristics using VADER showed significantly lower scores for hallucination reports associated with these reviews.

methodologies.name: Mixed-methods LLM hallucination analysis pipeline
methodologies.description: A mixed-methods pipeline applying a heuristic-based detection algorithm, manual annotation, N-gram generation, Non-Negative Matrix Factorization (NMF) topic modeling, and VADER sentiment analysis to user reviews.
datasets: 3 million user reviews from 90 AI-powered mobile apps

limitations.text: There is limited empirical understanding of how users perceive, report, and are impacted by LLM hallucinations in real-world mobile app settings.

future_work.text: Development of targeted monitoring and mitigation strategies for AI mobile apps.
